Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 44, English)
The Three Kinds of Negativity: Open, Sent, and Pitru-Routed

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn Mool T atva satsang continuing the ongoing Surya V igyan/ener gy-bonding series, focused specifically on classifying negativity below the devta yoni into thr ee distinct operational categories — how each one actually r eaches a tar get and why — closing with an extended, unpr ompted live tribute fr om sangat members describing their personal experience of the ashram and Bhaiya's six years of sustained tapasya.
1. Why This Classification Matters

1. Bhaiya opens by briefly r ecapping the series so far (stages of bhakti, how energy forms bonds, and the Surya Vigyan theory taught pr eviously) befor e turning to today's specific topic: classifying negativity below the devta yoni into clear , learnable categories. 2. The stated purpose is explicitly practical: this teaching states that a person must understand negativity's actual rules in order to eventually pr otect themselves and their family independently , rather than r emaining permanently dependent on visiting dhams (shrines) or specific individuals for every futur e crisis — including crises that may af fect one's own future children. 3. Bhaiya states plainly that even destructive tantrik kriya (maaran kriya) can be counter ed quickly by those with advanced, activated drishti — the entire aim of Ashaeiynn is for a practitioner to personally become capable enough, through their own tapobal and guru's grace, to protect both themselves and their family without outside dependency .
2. How Negativity Forms: The Six Root Flaws and the "Ratio" of Impurity

1. This teaching states that negativity in general forms ar ound an extr eme dominance of one of the six r oot flaws — kaam (lust), krodh (anger), lobh (gr eed), mad (pride), moh (attachment), or matsar (envy) — a person with extreme dominant kaam, for instance, becomes a pret carrying that same dominant quality after death, and the same principle applies in parallel across all six flaws. 2. An illustrative analogy is offer ed: just as feeding one person only milk, another only r oti, and another only onion changes each person's internal "tattva" despite them starting fr om the same basic human form, differ ences in accumulated internal energy similarly determine which specific yoni (pr et, pishach, pishachini, rakshasni, brahmrakshasni, dakini, shakini, and so on) a negativity ultimately takes. 3. This teaching clarifies that these varied names don't r epresent fundamentally separate categories of being — they simply r eflect different "ratios" (mixtur es) of malinta (impurity) accumulated internally , much like differing proportions of the same basic ingr edients.
3. Why Knowing the Specific Type of Negativity Matters Practically

1. A practical analogy is offer ed: if you know one r oom contains excess trash and another contains excess soil, you bring a trash-collector for one and a shovel for the other — the specific "container"/tool needed depends entir ely on corr ectly

identifying what you'r e actually dealing with. 2. The key practical takeaway: once you know pr ecisely what type of negativity you'r e facing, you can either construct the appr opriate countermeasur e yourself, or , as Bhaiya jokes, simply "order it from Amazon" — the critical first step is always corr ect identification.
4. Category One: Open (Khuli) Negativity — Self-Arising Through Natural Attraction

1. The first category is "open" negativity — negativity that arises pur ely thr ough natural attraction (kaam-vasna, hunger , or any other dominant internal drive) rather than being deliberately dir ected by anyone. If a person lacks any protective bandhan (binding/shield) or spiritual security , such negativity can attach itself relatively easily . 2. This teaching states that young women ar e especially vulnerable to this category , describing them semi-jokingly as a "highly endanger ed species" — since male pr ets (and even living elderly men, per this teaching's observation) ar e frequently drawn toward them, and even a deceased mother -in-law's personal grudge against a daughter -in-law can persist and act against her after death. 3. This is offer ed as a specific, concr ete explanation for a common pattern: new brides experiencing pr ogr essively worsening unexplained aches (hands, feet, back) after marriage, attributed to a household's own pitru targeting the daughter -in-law out of r epressed desire or preexisting r esentment — invisible without drishti, and one of the specific reasons this teaching states such households often actively (if unconsciously) r esist any family member's drishti fr om opening, since that family member would immediately r ecognize and object to what's occurring.
5. Category Two: Sent (Bheji Hui) Negativity — Deliberately Dir ected via a Tantrik

1. The second category is negativity deliberately sent by someone with a personal grievance against a target. This teaching walks through a specific illustrative mechanism: a person who resents someone approaches a tantrik for help, rather than confronting the tar get directly (since direct physical harm risks legal consequences like an FIR). 2. The tantrik does not act dir ectly — instead, this teaching states they go to a cr emation gr ound and "hir e" an alr eadydeceased pr et through a bhog offering (functioning as a form of payment), pr omising the pr et elevated status, its own mantra, or eventual pr omotion to devta-level standing in exchange for carrying out the assignment against the specified target. 3. Because this sent pr et carries a portion of the tantrik's own mantra shakti, this teaching states it is considerably mor e powerful than an ordinary "open" negativity , and can affect a target's aura and pr oduce impact r elatively quickly .
6. Concr ete Physical Effects of Sent Negativity

1. This teaching lists a range of specific physical effects associated with sent (tantrik-dir ected) negativity: pr essure on the chest, pressure on the thr oat, and various forms of physical constriction. 2. A specific, recognizable pattern described: suddenly "blanking out" mid-task (talking or working, then abruptly losing one's train of thought) — described as common and dir ectly attributable to this kind of interfer ence, not simply ordinary forgetfulness. 3. Another specific pattern: falling suddenly and inexplicably asleep specifically when attempting one particular task (for example, only when sitting down to study), while r emaining otherwise fully alert and capable for all other activities — this teaching states this points to a specific, tar geted attack on that particular activity , not general tiredness. 4. This teaching confirms that physical attacks specifically intensifying on amavasya (the new moon) ar e real and dir ectly attributable to a combination of pitru influence and black magic — and states plainly that these ar e treatable, with a direct assurance ("I guarantee you") that pr oper treatment r esolves them.
7. Category Three: Pitru-Routed Infiltration — Recruiting an "Insider" Against Pr otected Households

1. The third category specifically targets well-pr otected households — those wher e an actively worshipped devta maintains a visible pr otective "guard" pr esence. Since an ordinary outside pret cannot easily bypass this security , this teaching states a

tantrik instead specifically recruits an already-deceased member of that same family (an existing household pitru) to act as an inside operative. 2. The mechanism: since this r ecruited pitru was alr eady , historically , a legitimate member of that specific household, it can bypass the devta's pr otective guards far mor e easily than an unr elated outside entity — the guards r ecognize it as belonging ther e. 3. This teaching describes the r ecruited pitru being offer ed the same kind of bhog-based incentive (pr omised elevated status, mantra, or eventual pr omotion) in exchange for infiltrating the household and enabling a secondary negativity to enter alongside it — illustrated by a "friend" analogy: the pitru leads the secondary negativity in as if intr oducing a trusted companion, at which point the attack is sprung fr om within, past defenses that would have stopped an outsider . 4. This teaching states this specific mechanism is pr ecisely why victims in such cases often cannot identify any clear external cause for their distress — they assume it is simply generic, unexplained "negativity ," without r ealizing their own household pitru ar e the ones actually r esponsible for enabling or directly causing it.
8. Practical Guidance: Keep Pitru at a Respectful Distance, Don't Try to "Purify" Them

1. This teaching's practical closing guidance r estates a r ecurring theme: don't attempt to actively "purify" or cleanse one's pitru through worship, since a purified pitru will simply become impur e again on its own, in time, r egardless. 2. An illustrative analogy: just as putting on clean clothes today doesn't guarantee they'll stay clean for ever without ongoing self-maintenance, a person shouldn't expect someone else to keep "r e-dressing" them indefinitely — either maintain the boundary yourself going forward, or ask the sour ce of the pr oblem to leave the space entir ely , rather than repeating a temporary fix indefinitely .
9. Bhaiya's Teaching Pace and Session Philosophy

1. Bhaiya explicitly states his intention to build on this classification gradually acr oss futur e sessions rather than overwhelming the sangat with everything at once, noting his own pr eference (shar ed by the sangat, per his framing) to absorb teaching in comfortable stages while continuing consistent japa and devotion to Bhagwan's name in the meantime.
10. Bhaiya's Personal Reflection: Six Years Without a Human Guru, and Rapid Recent Gr owth

1. In response to extended live gratitude fr om sangat members (see Part III), Bhaiya r eflects candidly that during his own original six years of sadhna, he took no human guru at all, believing only a dir ect manifestation of Hanuman Ji Maharaj himself would count as genuine attainment — his own drishti did not open for the full six years even as, by his own account, many others' did during that same period. 2. Once Prabhu did manifest and grant him the fuller range of vidyas, Bhaiya states he told Prabhu dir ectly that futur e devotees would not need to wait nearly as long for the same darshan — and this teaching frames Ashaeiynn's curr ent, comparatively rapid pace of opening others' drishti (citing r oughly one new person's drishti opening per week since the institute's founding ar ound the pr evious Mar ch) as the dir ect, ongoing fulfillment of that stated intention. 3. Bhaiya states he considers every mantra, vidya, and siddhi he now teaches to be entir ely his guru's grace and instruction, not his own personal accomplishment, and that a disciple's cor e duty toward a guru is simply never to fall in that guru's estimation.
1 1. A Specific Devotional Instruction: Bowing Twice, and Dedicating Jaap in Bhaiya's Pr esence

1. Bhaiya makes a specific, dir ect request of the sangat: whenever they encounter or think of his own guru (Hanuman Ji Maharaj), to bow twice — once for themselves, and once on Bhaiya's own behalf. 2. He further states a specific devotional formula and a dir ect promise attached to it: when a practitioner mentally invokes, "In the pr esence of Parikshit Bhaiya, I dedicate my jaap to Hanuman Ji Maharaj," while tr eating Bhaiya as a
witness (sakshi) to their practice, this teaching pr omises that the practitioner will directly per ceive a subtle body immediately beside them, chanting "Sita Ram" in support.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Negativity below the devta yoni falls into thr ee distinct operational categories: open (self-arising thr ough natural attraction), sent (deliberately dir ected by someone via a tantrik), and pitru-r outed (infiltrating pr otected households through a r ecruited, alr eady-deceased family member). Different negativity "types" (pr et, pishach, pishachini, rakshasni, brahm-rakshasni, dakini, shakini) ar e not fundamentally separate categories of being — they simply reflect dif ferent ratios/mixtures of internally accumulated malinta (impurity), determined by which of the six root flaws (kaam, krodh, lobh, mad, moh, matsar) dominated in life. Corr ectly identifying the specific type of negativity affecting someone is the essential first step to countering it — the appropriate countermeasure depends entirely on accurate identification, much like needing the right tool for a specific kind of mess. Open negativity arises fr om natural attraction wher e no pr otective bandhan exists — young women ar e described as especially vulnerable to this category , including from a household's own pitru harboring repressed desire or resentment, which this teaching of fers as a concrete explanation for otherwise-unexplained new-bride aches and pains. Sent negativity is deliberately arranged thr ough a tantrik, who "hir es" an alr eady-deceased pr et via a cr emationgr ound bhog offering in exchange for promised status, mantra, or promotion — because it carries a portion of the tantrik's own mantra shakti, it is considerably more powerful than open negativity , producing ef fects like chest/throat pressure, sudden mid-task "blanking out," and task-specific sudden sleepiness (notably worsening on amavasya). Pitru-routed infiltration specifically targets well-pr otected, actively-worshipped households — a tantrik r ecruits an existing family pitru (which can bypass devta guards mor e easily than an outsider) to enable a secondary negativity's entry , which is why victims in these cases often can't identify a clear external cause and mistakenly assume it's just generic negativity . Don't attempt to actively "purify" one's own pitru thr ough r epeated worship — a purified pitru simply becomes impur e again over time regardless; either maintain healthy boundaries dir ectly , or ask the sour ce of the pr oblem to leave entirely , rather than r epeating a temporary fix indefinitely . Bhaiya spent his own original six years of sadhna without any human guru, believing only Hanuman Ji Maharaj's direct manifestation would count as genuine attainment — after Prabhu eventually appeared and taught him fully , Bhaiya committed to ensuring future devotees would not need to wait nearly as long, which this teaching frames as the reason for Ashaeiynn's currently rapid pace of opening others' drishti. A specific devotional instruction: bow twice whenever encountering Bhaiya's guru (once for yourself, once on Bhaiya's behalf), and mentally dedicate your jaap "in the pr esence of Parikshit Bhaiya" to Hanuman Ji Maharaj — this teaching promises this will bring a subtle body to chant "Sita Ram" directly beside the practitioner . Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 44, English)
The Three Kinds of Negativity: Open, Sent, and Pitru-Routed
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn live session. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. Why is it important to classify negativity into differ ent types? A: Per this teaching, a person must understand negativity's actual rules in order to eventually protect themselves and their family independently — rather than remaining permanently dependent on dhams or specific individuals for every future crisis, including crises that may one day af fect their own children.

Q2. Can advanced practitioners actually counter serious black magic (maaran kriya) quickly? A: Yes — per this teaching, those with advanced, activated drishti can counter even destructive tantrik kriya quickly; the entire aim of Ashaeiynn is for practitioners to personally become capable of protecting themselves and their family without outside dependency .

Q3. What actually determines whether a negative entity becomes a "pr et," "pishach," "rakshasni," or some other type? A: Per this teaching, it depends on which of the six root flaws (kaam, krodh, lobh, mad, moh, matsar) was most dominant, and the specific "ratio" of accumulated malinta (impurity) — these varied names aren't fundamentally separate categories of being, just dif ferent mixtures of the same underlying impurity , similar to how dif ferent foods change a person's internal tattva despite them starting from the same basic form.

Q4. Why does it matter so much to corr ectly identify the specific type of negativity affecting someone? A: Because, per this teaching's own analogy , the appropriate countermeasure depends entirely on accurate identification — like needing a trash-collector for a room full of trash versus a shovel for a room full of soil. Once you know precisely what you're dealing with, you can build (or otherwise obtain) the right tool to address it.

Q5. What is "open" (khuli) negativity? A: The first of three categories — negativity that arises purely through natural attraction (like kaam-vasna or hunger) rather than being deliberately sent by anyone; it can attach relatively easily to someone lacking any protective bandhan or spiritual security .

Q6. Why ar e young women described as especially vulnerable to open negativity? A: Per this teaching, male prets (and even living elderly men, by this teaching's observation) are frequently drawn toward them, and even a deceased mother -in-law's personal grudge can persist and act against a daughter -in-law after death — this teaching semi-jokingly describes young women as a "highly endangered species" in this specific sense.

Q7. Why do many new brides experience worsening unexplained pain after marriage, according to this teaching? A: This teaching attributes a common pattern of progressively worsening aches (hands, feet, back) to household pitru tar geting the daughter -inlaw out of repressed desire or resentment — invisible without drishti, and part of why such households often resist any family member's drishti opening.

Q8. What is "sent" (bheji hui) negativity? A: The second category — negativity deliberately arranged by someone with a personal grievance against a tar get, typically via a tantrik rather than direct confrontation (which risks legal consequences).

Q9. How does a tantrik actually "send" negativity against someone, per this teaching? A: The tantrik goes to a cremation ground and "hires" an already-deceased pret through a bhog of fering (functioning as payment), promising elevated status, its own mantra, or eventual promotion to devta-level standing in exchange for carrying out the assignment against the specified tar get.

Q10. Why is sent negativity consider ed mor e danger ous than open negativity? A: Because it carries a portion of the tantrik's own mantra shakti, per this teaching, making it considerably more powerful and capable of af fecting a tar get's aura and producing impact relatively quickly .

Q1 1. What ar e some concr ete physical effects associated with sent (tantrik-dir ected) negativity? A: This teaching lists chest pressure, throat pressure, and various forms of physical constriction, along with sudden mid-task "blanking out" and task-specific sudden sleepiness (for example, only when sitting down to study , while remaining alert for everything else).

Q12. Do attacks fr om this kind of negativity r eally intensify on amavasya (the new moon)? A: Yes — this teaching confirms this pattern is real and directly attributable to a combination of pitru influence and black magic, while stating plainly that it is treatable, with a direct assurance that proper treatment resolves it.

Q13. What is "pitru-r outed" negativity , the third category? A: Negativity that specifically tar gets well-protected households (those with an actively worshipped devta maintaining a visible protective guard) by recruiting an already-deceased member of that same family as an inside operative, since an outside pret cannot easily bypass such security .

Q14. Why can a r ecruited family pitru bypass a household's pr otective guards mor e easily than an outside entity? A: Because, per this teaching, the recruited pitru was historically a legitimate member of that specific household, so the devta's protective guards recognize it as belonging there and allow it through more easily than an unrelated outsider .

Q15. How does the r ecruited pitru actually enable an attack once inside? A: Per this teaching's "friend" analogy , the pitru leads a secondary negativity in as if introducing a trusted companion, and the attack is sprung from within — past defenses that would have stopped an outsider entirely .

Q16. Why do victims of pitru-r outed negativity often not r ealize what's actually happening? A: Because, per this teaching, they typically assume their distress is just generic, unexplained "negativity ," without realizing their own household pitru are the ones actually responsible for enabling or directly causing it.

Q17. Should I try to actively "purify" or cleanse my own tr oublesome pitru thr ough worship? A: This teaching advises against it — a purified pitru will simply become impure again over time regardless, similar to how clean clothes don't stay clean forever without ongoing self-maintenance; either maintain healthy boundaries yourself, or ask the source of the problem to leave entirely , rather than repeating a temporary fix indefinitely .

Q18. Will Bhaiya explain every r emaining detail of these thr ee categories in a single session? A: No — Bhaiya explicitly states his intention to build on this classification gradually across future sessions, preferring to teach in comfortable stages rather than overwhelm the sangat all at once.

Q19. Did Bhaiya have a human guru during his own original years of sadhna? A: No — per this teaching, during his own original six years of sadhna, he took no human guru at all, believing only a direct manifestation of Hanuman Ji Maharaj himself would count as genuine attainment; his own drishti did not open for the full six years even as, by his account, many others' did during that same period.

Q20. What did Bhaiya tell Prabhu once his own drishti finally opened? A: That future devotees would not need to wait nearly as long for the same darshan — this teaching frames Ashaeiynn's current, comparatively rapid pace of opening others' drishti (citing roughly one new person's drishti opening per week since the institute's founding) as the direct, ongoing fulfillment of that stated intention.

Q21. Does Bhaiya consider his current abilities to be his own personal accomplishment? A: No — he states he considers every mantra, vidya, and siddhi he now teaches to be entirely his guru's grace and instruction, framing a disciple's core duty as simply never
falling in that guru's estimation.

Q22. What specific devotional practice does Bhaiya ask of the sangat r egarding his own guru? A: To bow twice whenever they encounter or think of Hanuman Ji Maharaj — once for themselves, and once on Bhaiya's own behalf.

Q23. What happens if I mentally dedicate my jaap "in the pr esence of Parikshit Bhaiya" to Hanuman Ji Maharaj? A: This teaching promises that treating Bhaiya as a witness (sakshi) to this dedication will bring a subtle body directly beside the practitioner , chanting "Sita Ram" in support.
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 44 additions)

Always keep the three negativity categories (open, sent, pitru-routed) distinct and clearly labeled when discussing this teaching — never blur them into a single generic "negativity" concept, since this teaching's entire point is that correct classification determines the correct countermeasure. When explaining the dif ferent negativity "type" names (pret, pishach, pishachini, rakshasni, brahm-rakshasni, dakini, shakini), preserve the teaching's own framing that these are ratios/mixtures of impurity rather than fundamentally separate species — avoid presenting them as a fixed taxonomic hierarchy . Handle the "young women as an endangered species" and new-bride physical-symptom claims with care — present them as this teaching's own observational framing, and note that persistent unexplained physical pain should also be discussed with a qualified medical professional. Preserve the specific mechanism of "sent" negativity (tantrik hiring a pret via cremation-ground bhog, promised status/mantra/promotion) accurately and distinctly from "pitru-routed" negativity (recruiting an existing family member specifically to bypass devta guards) — these are dif ferent mechanisms serving dif ferent purposes (general tar geting vs. bypassing protected households). Keep the "don't try to purify your pitru, maintain distance instead" guidance consistent with prior sessions' pitru teachings (Sessions 39, 41, 43) — this is a recurring, stable principle across this teaching's body of work. Present Bhaiya's personal six-year no-human-guru account, and his stated commitment to accelerating others' path, as his own biographical reflection — of fered as inspiration and context, not as a claim that every practitioner's timeline will match his. Preserve the specific devotional instruction (bow twice; dedicate jaap "in the presence of Parikshit Bhaiya") accurately and exactly as stated, including the promised result (a subtle body chanting "Sita Ram" beside the practitioner) — present this as this teaching's own specific practice, not a universally required ritual. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
